payload.comment_body:
## Build Update

Evidence-only run: this re-entry removed the single leaked Faktorial result-envelope file committed in the assigned revision; no product implementation changed.

The committed delivery remains the cross-platform Makefile/make.cmd quality contract, Pages workflow alignment, and README guidance. Static checks passed: `git diff --check main...HEAD`; GNU Make dry-run expands typecheck, test, then build; Windows missing-worktree and unknown-target guards each exit 2 with clear guidance. No runtime notes, ADR, rule, or frontend asset changes apply. Canonical typecheck, tests, and build are intentionally deferred to Faktorial's `run-quality` verifier.

pull_request_description.delivered_outcome: A repository-owned cross-platform build and test contract for Faktorial workers, contributors, and GitHub Pages publishing.
pull_request_description.implementation_approach: Added aligned Makefile and make.cmd targets for deterministic worktree setup, typecheck, tests, production build, and fail-fast quality; routed Pages through that gate and documented the commands.
pull_request_description.solution_rationale: A single repository-defined entry point keeps fresh worktrees, local development, and CI on the same validation sequence while preserving existing npm scripts and deployment behavior.
pull_request_description.tradeoffs_and_alternatives: The adapters deliberately wrap existing npm scripts instead of replacing tooling or changing dependencies. GNU Make serves portable environments and make.cmd gives Windows an explicit native entry point.
pull_request_description.architectural_decisions:
The repository now treats `quality` as the canonical publishing and verification contract.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  W[Worktree] --> Q[quality]
  C[Contributor] --> Q
  P[Pages CI] --> Q
  Q --> T[Typecheck]
  Q --> S[Tests]
  Q --> B[Production build]
```
